data.claim: A tools/list request logged AFTER the OUT notifications/tools/list_changed line (and after the tool call that caused it) means the client honours list_changed; its absence means ignores
data.falsifier: An honouring driver and an ignoring driver produce logs the rule cannot tell apart
data.mechanism: The server only sees traffic; a client that refetches must send tools/list again
data.probe: Appendix A probe driven by a scripted honouring client (refetch after notification) and an ignoring one
data.probe_output: honour.log: IN tools/list id4 at 791.55 after OUT list_changed at 791.25; ignore.log ends at OUT list_changed with no later IN tools/list
data.question: Can a probe server's log alone classify a client as honouring list_changed?

chunk_findings.detail: `main` does `delay = float(args[k + 1])` without checking that `--delay` has a following argument. Running `python -m ddflow.mcpshim.probe_server probe.log --delay` raises `IndexError` and dumps a traceback instead of printing the usage message and returning `2`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:178

chunk_findings.detail: On `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, `probe_row` returns `unavailable` before ever reading `probe.log` or calling `analyze_log`. A client that successfully sends `list_changed`/discovers the new tool but then hangs until the timeout will have already produced dispositive evidence in `probe.log`; the function still reports `{"list_changed": "unavailable", "reason": "timed out after ..."}` and deletes the log with `TemporaryDirectory`, so a real `honours`/`ignores` result is lost. Correct behavior would be to read the available log in the timeout path and classify whatever was recorded before treating the timeout as unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:110

chunk_findings.detail: The test name says it verifies every unknown cell, and the intent lists `antigravity`, `grok build`, `windsurf`, `amp`, and `droid` in addition to the asserted set `{"codex","gemini","qwen","kimi","opencode","cursor","copilot"}`. The assertion only checks that subset, so a `matrix` subcommand that omits one of the untested unknown cells (for example, drops `droid`) still passes because the test neither requires that key nor fails when it is missing.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py:test_matrix_lists_every_unknown_cell_and_never_passes_a_missing_one

chunk_findings.detail: `read_until(want_id)` appends notifications to `self.notes` when `want_id is not None` but never returns buffered notifications when `want_id is None`. In `test_bump_adds_a_tool_and_notifies_at_once`, if the server sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` before the response to the `tools/call` `bump` request (a valid JSON-RPC ordering), `c.call("tools/call", {"name":"bump"})` consumes the notification into `self.notes` and returns the response. The subsequent `c.read_until(None)` then blocks forever on `self.p.stdout.readline()`, hanging the test suite instead of failing.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py:Client.read_until

data.body: SU-client-probe-ci shipped the probe server, classifier and scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe only: a 'mcp probe-client <harness>' verb changes the pinned CLI surface (mcp is a leaf command today), so it is split out. Settle also: write the client-table row into the table module (SU-client-table) rather than only printing JSON.
data.title: ddflow mcp probe-client CLI verb over scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe

chunk_findings.detail: When `delaybump` is called, `_call` appends `_ADDED` immediately and then starts `_later`, which only sleeps and sends the `notifications/tools/list_changed`; it never adds the tool. So a `tools/list` request before the configured delay already contains `secret_oracle`, even though the module doc, the `delaybump` description, and the intent all describe the tool being added “a few seconds LATER” / “6 s later.” The correct sequence is to append `_ADDED` inside `_later` just before sending the notification, not in `_call`. With the current ordering, the delayed-add path does not exercise what it advertises.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:_call

chunk_findings.detail: `serve` only catches `ValueError` around `probe.handle(json.loads(line))`, but syntactically valid JSON can produce a non-dict, such as `null` (the line `null\n`). `probe.handle(None)` then calls `None.get` and raises `AttributeError`, killing the single handler thread; queued valid requests after that line are never answered while stdin remains open. `analyze_log` has the same problem at `meth = m.get("method")` if the logged line is valid non-dict JSON. The code should check `isinstance(m, dict)` before handling/analyzing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:serve

chunk_findings.detail: The matrix subcommand iterates `PENDING` and will emit JSON keys `copilot` and `grok`, but the change’s intent names these UNKNOWN cells as `copilot cli` and `grok build`. If the matrix in `docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md` is keyed by the intent’s cell names, `scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe matrix` never emits/updates those two cells and instead reports two different keys (`copilot`, `grok`), so the intended coverage is still missed.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:73,75

chunk_findings.detail: `probe_row` misclassifies a missing API key/credentials as `unknown`, not `unavailable`. Input: `claude` is on PATH but `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset or no Claude credentials exist; the CLI exits non-zero without ever connecting to the probe server, so `probe.log` is empty. `analyze_log("")` yields `list_changed == "unknown"`, and the branch at line 123 returns that row with exit 2. The intent says missing key is `unavailable`; the resulting matrix row is therefore `unknown`, losing the coverage-gap distinction.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:123

chunk_findings.detail: The test enforces “never discloses the new tool name” only by asserting `"secret_oracle" not in json.dumps(r)` for the `tools/call` `bump` response. It then reads the `notifications/tools/list_changed` notification into `note`, but never asserts `"secret_oracle" not in json.dumps(note)`. A probe server that sends a clean `bump` response but leaks the new tool name in the list_changed notification will still pass this test, despite violating the documented intent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py:test_bump_adds_a_tool_and_notifies_at_once

chunk_findings.detail: `delaybump` sends the same tool result text as `bump`: “server tool list changed (new tool name not disclosed; list your tools to find it)”. A client that obeys that result (for example an agent calling `delaybump` with the cheap-model prompt) will emit `tools/list` immediately, then the 6-second delayed `notifications/tools/list_changed` arrives later. The log becomes `IN tools/call delaybump`, `OUT tools/call result`, `IN tools/list`, then later `OUT notifications/tools/list_changed`. `analyze_log` sees no `tools/list` after the notification and returns `list_changed: "ignores"`, even though the client is only following the probe’s own instruction before the notification has been sent. This makes the `delaybump` row falsely report an ignoring client and reduces the matrix to an artifact of the result text; a client that would refetch on `list_changed` can be marked `ignores`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:_Probe._call / analyze_log

chunk_findings.detail: When an installed CLI is present on PATH but its API key is missing or expired, `shutil.which` succeeds, so the function never marks the row `unavailable`. The subprocess exits nonzero before the MCP probe can produce a useful log; `analyze_log("")` yields `list_changed == "unknown"`, and the function returns `{"list_changed": "unknown", ...}` with exit code 2. This violates the change's explicit requirement that "missing CLI/key = unavailable, never pass": the row is reported as an inconclusive `unknown` rather than an `unavailable` coverage gap, so CI cannot distinguish a missing key from a model that simply did not call the probe.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:probe_row

chunk_findings.detail: This test writes the `tools/call bump` and a `tools/list` request in a single stdin write, then asserts `_analyze()(c.close())["list_changed"] == "ignores"`. That outcome depends on the probe server logging the second `tools/list` line before it emits `notifications/tools/list_changed` for the `bump`. If the server is a normal synchronous stdin loop (read one request, handle it, write the notification, read the next request), the notification is logged before the pipelined `tools/list`, so the analyzer returns `honours` and the assertion fails. Even with a separate reader thread the ordering is a scheduling race between the reader logging the second line and the handler emitting the notification; the test cannot deterministically guarantee the docstring claim from the server log.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py:test_a_pipelined_tools_list_is_logged_before_the_notification

chunk_findings.detail: For any `tools/call` whose `name` is not `bump` or `delaybump`, the `else` branch returns `"MAGENTA"` without checking whether that tool is actually in `self.tools`. Input: a client sends `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"secret_oracle"}}` immediately after `initialize`, before `bump`/`delaybump`; the server responds `MAGENTA` even though `_ADDED` documents the tool as “Only exists after bump or delaybump.” This lets a client obtain the probe’s secret answer without the tool ever having been exposed through `tools/list`, undermining the probe’s controlled condition and potentially producing a false “honours discover” result.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:_call

chunk_findings.detail: `IN_LIMIT = 2000` truncates every request before it is written to the log. A valid JSON-RPC `initialize` request longer than 2000 characters (for example a large `capabilities`/`experimental` object) is written as invalid truncated JSON. `_parse` skips invalid lines, so `analyze_log` returns `client: None`, `revision: None` even though the client did initialize and negotiate, losing the client version and protocol revision fields the intent requires in the matrix row.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:log_in

chunk_findings.detail: Once `_ADDED` is already in `self.tools`, subsequent `bump`/`delaybump` calls still send `notifications/tools/list_changed` even though the tool list did not change. Input: call `bump` twice; the second call sends a `list_changed` notification for a no-op change because `_call` does not guard the notification on whether an actual append occurred. This violates MCP list_changed semantics and can cause a client to refetch and find no new tool, adding spurious traffic to the probe.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:_call and _later

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 3 still holds for `copilot`: the tuple has `"copilot"` and `"grok-build"`, but the intent and the matrix cell names are `"copilot cli"` and `"grok build"`. The `matrix` loop used by `probe_row(h)` emits JSON keys taken directly from this tuple, so a consumer keyed by `copilot cli`/`grok build` never receives/updates those cells. The current change only added the hyphen to `grok` and left `copilot` unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:PENDING

chunk_findings.detail: When the CLI exits 0 and `analyze_log(text)` yields `list_changed == "unknown"` (the model never called the probe), the branch returns `row` with `"list_changed": "unknown"` and exit code 2. The module doc says exit 2 is “could not run … or the model never called the probe” and that `unavailable` is a coverage gap. Example: a `claude` wrapper on PATH that exits 0 without writing `probe.log` produces `{"harness":"claude","list_changed":"unknown",...}`; it should be `unavailable`, otherwise the matrix presents an actually untested cell as merely unknown rather than as a coverage gap.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:probe_row

chunk_findings.detail: `row` and `matrix` only do `print(json.dumps(...))`; neither opens nor writes `docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md`. The script’s own docstring and the change intent say a row is written to that matrix file, but running `scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe row claude` leaves the markdown file unchanged. No documented/external writer is invoked, so the productised table is not actually updated by this change.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:main

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 3 still holds: the unknown-cell set asserts `"copilot"` and `"grok-build"` are present, but the change's intent names those cells `"copilot cli"` and `"grok build"`. With this test, a matrix subcommand that never emits/updates `copilot cli` or `grok build` (but emits `copilot` and `grok-build`) passes, so the intended coverage is still missed; the added regression does not answer the key mismatch.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py:test_matrix_lists_every_unknown_cell_and_never_passes_a_missing_one

chunk_findings.detail: The “never discloses the new tool name” requirement is not enforced for the delayed path. The test checks `"list your tools" not in json.dumps(r)` but never asserts `"secret_oracle"` is absent from the `delaybump` response or from the delayed `notifications/tools/list_changed` it later reads. A probe that replies to `delaybump` with text containing `"secret_oracle will appear later"` (or leaks it in the notification) passes all delaybump tests, violating the stated intent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py:test_delaybump_adds_the_tool_only_when_it_notifies

chunk_findings.detail: `bump` returns `REFETCH_HINT`, which explicitly tells the client/model to call `tools/list`. A client that does not honor `notifications/tools/list_changed` at all but does obey that tool result will emit `tools/list` after the server writes the result and the notification back-to-back, so `analyze_log` sees `IN tools/list` after the `OUT notifications/tools/list_changed` line and reports `list_changed: 'honours'`. This makes the `bump` path classify a notification-ignoring CLI as honoring, contradicting the module’s own rule that `honours iff the log shows tools/list AFTER the notification`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:_call (bump branch)

chunk_findings.detail: `shutil.which(rec["bin"])` can return a relative pathname when the command is found through a relative PATH entry (for example `PATH="."` and an executable `kilo` in the current directory). The function then runs `subprocess.run(argv, cwd=work)`, where `work` is a fresh temp directory, so the relative executable is resolved against the temp dir, does not exist there, and `subprocess.run` raises `FileNotFoundError`. The script crashes with a traceback instead of printing an `unavailable` row. Rebasing `binary` to an absolute path before use would avoid this.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:probe_row

chunk_findings.detail: The `analyze` subcommand always returns 0. Given an empty log file, `analyze_log("")` produces `{"list_changed": "unknown"}`, so `scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe analyze empty.log` prints an inconclusive row and still exits 0. The script's own contract says exit 0 means concluded, and the `row`/`matrix` paths return non-zero for `unknown`; a caller consuming the exit status will mistake an unknown classification for a concluded/passing result.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:main (analyze branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that a follow-up `tools/list` sent immediately after `delaybump` returns does not yet include `secret_oracle`. That assertion depends on the 0.5s delayed timer not firing before the server processes that follow-up request. On a loaded CI machine the timer can fire after the `tools/list` request is queued but before the server responds to it; the response then legitimately includes `secret_oracle`, causing the first absence assertion to fail even though the server followed the intended notify-on-add behavior. This wall-clock delay makes the test nondeterministic.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py:test_delaybump_adds_the_tool_only_when_it_notifies

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 2 still holds for larger valid messages. `IN_LIMIT = 65536` still truncates every incoming line, and `_parse` skips lines whose truncated JSON is invalid. A valid `initialize` request of, for example, 100,000 characters is logged as a 65536-character invalid JSON fragment; `analyze_log` then returns `"client": None` and `"revision": None` even though the client did initialize and negotiate. The fix only moved the cutoff from 2000 to 65536 and does not answer the defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:log_in

chunk_findings.detail: `OUT_LIMIT = 300` truncates every outgoing logged message. After `bump`, a server `tools/list` response containing the full tool list is much longer than 300 characters; the logged JSON is cut mid-object and is invalid, so `_parse` drops it. The module docstring says the probe “logs every message,” but outgoing server messages are not actually logged fully. The current `analyze_log` only needs the short `notifications/tools/list_changed` note, so the matrix row is not affected, but the advertised logging guarantee is still false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:send

chunk_findings.detail: `_unavailable` returns only `{"harness", "list_changed", "reason"}`, but the module’s row contract at the top says every row includes `"client"`, `"revision"`, `"probed_discover"`, and `"listen"` (only `"reason"` is optional). The `probe_row` unknown branches call `_unavailable` after `analyze_log` has already parsed the initialize line, discarding a known `client`/`revision`. For example, a `claude` that sends `initialize` with `client=claude`, `revision=1.0` and then exits 1 before calling `bump` produces `{"harness": "claude", "list_changed": "unavailable", "reason": "exit 1 before the probe ran: ..."}`; the negotiated version/revision are lost from the printed row, violating the documented row shape.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:_unavailable

chunk_findings.detail: The new tests execute the production `row`/`matrix` subcommands with `cwd=ROOT` and no isolation of the markdown destination. The change contract, and the triage for previous finding 6, say `scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe` now writes `docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md`. Running `test_matrix_lists_every_unknown_cell_and_never_passes_a_missing_one` with `_run("matrix", env={"PATH": str(tmp_path)})` will therefore overwrite the repository’s real matrix file with a full table of `unavailable` rows; `test_missing_cli_is_unavailable_exit_2` and the other `_run("row", ...)` tests likewise write rows into the tracked file. The test suite must use a temp output path or a `--dry-run`/env override so it does not dirty the working tree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py:_run / test_matrix_lists_every_unknown_cell_and_never_passes_a_missing_one

chunk_findings.detail: The previously reported delaybump/tools/list race still holds. `_later` calls `_add()` and then `send(NOTE)` in two separate locked sections, while the `tools/list` handler reads and passes the mutable `self.tools` list without taking a consistent snapshot. Interleaving: a client calls `delaybump`; after `time.sleep(self.delay)`, `_add()` appends `secret_oracle`; before `_later` reaches `send`, the consumer thread processes an already queued `tools/list`. That response now contains `secret_oracle` even though no `notifications/tools/list_changed` has been sent, violating the probe's stated “adds the tool only when it notifies” behavior and making the immediate-list check flaky or semantically wrong. The added `SETTLE_S` sleep does not fence the window between `_add` and `send`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:_later

chunk_findings.detail: The test still has the race called out in the prior review: it sends a follow-up `tools/list` immediately after `delaybump` and asserts `"secret_oracle" not in _tool_names(...)` before notification, relying only on `--delay 1.5`. A 1.5s timer does not make this deterministic. On a loaded CI runner, the server process can be descheduled after receiving the `tools/list` request but before it handles it; the timer thread can then fire and add `secret_oracle`, so the response legitimately contains it, failing the first absence assertion even though the server notified after receiving the request. The increase from 0.5 to 1.5 only lowers flake probability; it does not answer the prior finding. The test should block/queue the notification before issuing the first follow-up `tools/list`, or the server/fixture should provide a deterministic sync point.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py:test_delaybump_adds_the_tool_only_when_it_notifies

chunk_findings.detail: The handler’s only guarantee that a pipelined `tools/list` is logged before the notification is `time.sleep(SETTLE_S)`, with `SETTLE_S = 0.02`. A fixed sleep is not synchronization: if a client writes `tools/call bump` and `tools/list` back-to-back without waiting, the reader thread can log the first line and then be descheduled for more than 20 ms before reading the second. The handler thread then sleeps for 20 ms, handles `bump`, and `_add_and_notify()` sends/logs `OUT notifications/tools/list_changed` before the second line is logged as `IN tools/list`. `analyze_log` then returns `honours` even though the client sent the `tools/list` before the notification, making the CI matrix result nondeterministic under load.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:serve

chunk_findings.detail: The prompt instructs the model to `call lc bump`, but the probe server’s tool is `delaybump` (the name is visible in the previously reported interleaving and in `tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py::test_delaybump_adds_the_tool_only_when_it_notifies`). A CLI exposes `mcp__lc__delaybump`; there is no tool named `bump`. A cheap/literal model will reply that it cannot find `bump` and never invoke `delaybump`, so `analyze_log` returns `unknown` and `probe_row` reports `unavailable` for `claude`/`kilo` even when the client would actually honor `list_changed`. The probe is therefore nondeterministically false-negative whenever the model does not guess the fuzzy tool name.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:PROMPT

chunk_findings.detail: The test does not catch the confirmed race it was added for. It only verifies that `send` is called while `probe.lock` is held. That remains true if `_add_and_notify` is still two separate critical sections: `with self.lock: self._add()` then `with self.lock: self.send(NOTE)`, and the test would still assert `held == [True]`. The original interleaving — a consumer thread handling an already queued `tools/list` between `_add` and `send`, returning `secret_oracle` before the notification — remains possible and would not be caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_soft_probe.py:test_add_and_notify_are_one_step_under_the_lock

chunk_findings.detail: This test is flaky and/or the probe misclassifies the pipelined client. It writes the `bump` request and the following `tools/list` in a single `write`; after the reader enqueues `bump`, the consumer can handle `bump` and emit `notifications/tools/list_changed` before the reader logs the second request’s `IN` line (the second line may already buffered by `readline()` but not yet yielded to the loop). The log then shows a `tools/list` after the notification, so `_analyze()` returns `"honours"`, and the assertion `== "ignores"` fails depending on reader/consumer scheduling.

chunk_findings.detail: When the CLI exists, `subprocess.run` runs it, and it exits nonzero before the probe log reaches a conclusion, `probe_row` returns `unavailable` with exit code 2. The script’s own contract says exit 1 means “CLI ran and failed” and exit 2 means “could not run… coverage gap.” A CLI that actually ran and failed is not a coverage gap, so this hides a broken installed CLI/recipe as unavailable. Example: a bad `claude` flag causes `claude ...` to exit 64 with an empty probe log; `probe_row` returns `(list_changed="unavailable", code=2)` instead of code 1.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:136

chunk_findings.detail: The file’s docstring advertises every row as containing `"client"`, `"revision"`, `"probed_discover"`, and `"listen"`, but `_unavailable(harness, reason)` with no `seen` returns only `{"harness", "list_changed", "reason"}`. Any row emitted because a CLI is not on PATH and every PENDING cell therefore lacks the documented keys. Example: `scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe matrix` on a runner without `claude`/`kilo` prints a `"claude"` object with no `client`/`revision`/`probed_discover`/`listen`, so a downstream table writer that follows the advertised row contract and reads `row["client"]` will raise `KeyError`.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/ci/mcp-client-probe:_unavailable

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds. A fixed `time.sleep(SETTLE_S)` is not synchronization. If a client writes `tools/call bump` and `tools/list` back-to-back in one `write`, the reader thread can log the first `IN` line and then be descheduled for longer than 20 ms; the handler then sends/logs `notifications/tools/list_changed` before the second `IN tools/list` line. `analyze_log` will classify that pipelined client as `honours` even though the `tools/list` was sent before the client could have seen the notification. The docstring admission and “real runs are serial” do not remove the race.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/mcpshim/probe_server.py:serve

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds. The test is nondeterministic: after the single `c.p.stdin.write(...)` containing both `bump` and `tools/list`, the consumer can handle `bump` and log `OUT notifications/tools/list_changed` before the reader thread logs the second line as `IN`. In that interleaving the log shows `tools/list` after the notification, `_analyze()` returns `"honours"`, and the assertion `== "ignores"` fails. Passing 10/10 runs is not a fix for a descheduling window.

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds. The rewritten test still does not catch the split-lock mutant from the previous review. For a mutant `_add_and_notify` implemented as `with self.lock: self._add()` followed by `with self.lock: self.send(NOTE)`, `spy` is called while the send lock is held, so the snapshot thread still blocks, `state == ["blocked"]` still passes, and `ps._ADDED in snaps[0]` still passes. The test never places a snapshot in the interval between `_add()` and `send`, so the original race remains untested.
